changes.text: 马骡那一项更实际。格兰特当场给出的理由是过冬的收成：收缴来的牲口对联邦没用，对回家的小农是活下去的工具。一种解释是，这一项针对的不是面子，而是协议签完之后能不能真的收场——人要回乡、要吃饭、要种地，前面那些条款才有执行的人。要提醒的是，这一项不在已写成的条文里，是格兰特当面答应李、将指示留守军官办理的。

The horses and mules were the more practical item. The reason Grant gave on the spot was the winter crop: animals taken in surrender were of no use to the Union, but to small farmers going home they were the tools of survival. One reading is that this item addressed not face but whether the settlement could actually be wound up afterward — the men had to go home, eat, and plant, and only then were there people to carry out everything already written down. A caution: this was not in the terms as written; Grant told Lee he would instruct the officers left behind.
格兰特写明，他不知道李是什么心情。按他的描述，李神情庄重、喜怒不形于色，看不出是为战争终于结束而高兴，还是为结局难过而不肯表露。倒是他自己，收到信时满心欢喜，此刻却变得低落。

Grant was explicit that he did not know what Lee was feeling. In Grant's description, Lee was a man of much dignity with an impassible face; it was impossible to say whether he was inwardly glad the end had finally come, or sad at the result and too manly to show it. Whatever his feelings, they were entirely concealed from Grant's observation. Grant's own were a different matter: jubilant on receipt of the letter, he now found them sad and depressed.

dispositions.rationale: 英文的“this clause addressed”改为“this item addressed”。中文的“这一条针对的”改为“这一项针对的”，首句“马骡那条”也一并改为“马骡那一项”。马骡的宽许不在已写成的条文中，而是格兰特口头承诺、交由留守军官办理的，改后措辞与本段末尾的提醒以及证据一致。

evidence.quote: I told him that as the terms were written they would not
I would, therefore, instruct the officers I left behind to receive the paroles of his troops to let every man of the Confederate army who claimed to own a horse or mule take the animal to his home

dispositions.rationale: 英文在“Lee was a man of much dignity with an impassible face”前加上“In Grant's description,”，明确这是格兰特的描述而非叙述者的断言，与中文的“按他的描述”同步。中文字段未作改动，按规则一并给出全文。

evidence.quote: As he was a man of much dignity, with an impassible face, it was impossible to say
